messages:
sophie: Noticed something weird in the API ref: our error example for 429 shows `Retry-After: 1500` and the text says "milliseconds", but runtime returns seconds (e.g., `Retry-After: 1`). Customers & SDKs are getting confused — JS retry helper treats Retry-After as ms.

eddie: Oof. Runtime uses standard HTTP semantics (seconds). The bad examples came from an earlier internal experiment. We should fix docs and add an SDK migration note.

maria: Proposal: update the API ref examples to show `Retry-After: 1` (seconds) and add a one-line note: "Retry-After header is in seconds per RFC 7231". Also add a small SDK guidance section showing how to convert to ms for client retry timers: `retryDelayMs = Number(response.headers['retry-after']) * 1000`.

leo: Devex: JS helper currently consumes header as ms in `retryAfterMs` variable. That's a breaking semantic if we flip docs. We should patch the helper to accept seconds or ms (detect if >1000 assume ms? that's brittle). Safer: change helper to read header as seconds and multiply internally where needed, but ship a small patch.

maria: OK — we can update docs first (low-risk) and include a migration note saying: "If your client used Retry-After as milliseconds, update to multiply by 1000 (JS) or use the patched helper v1.2.3+."

sophie: I'll open a docs PR with corrected examples (curl + python + ts) and a short code snippet for conversion. Will also add a clarifying sentence in the OpenAPI error response section.

docs-bot: docs-bot: PR created -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/9941. Preview: https://deploy-preview-9941--docs.redwood.ai.

eddie: Quick nit: please show both header and Retry-After in the example response body for older clients (some proxies inject it into JSON). e.g., `{"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":1}` and mention which one is authoritative (header).

maria: Good call. I'll include that side-by-side and mark the body field as legacy. Add note: "Header takes precedence."

leo: I'll prepare a small JS patch for the retry helper: it will parse header as seconds if value <= 60, otherwise treat as ms to be conservative. Will add unit tests. Aim to release patch tomorrow.

devex-bot: devex-bot: Created helper PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex-js/pull/210. Tests included.

sophie: PR updated with eddie's body-example and the conversion snippet: `const seconds = Number(res.headers['retry-after']); const delayMs = Number.isNaN(seconds) ? fallbackMs : seconds * 1000;` Added harness test asserting the preview shows `Retry-After: 1` in header.

docs-bot: docs-bot: preview tests passed. Examples render with seconds units.

eddie: LGTM. One last request: add a short note in the troubleshooting section: "If you see very large Retry-After values, confirm whether a proxy or CDN rewrote the header into ms."

maria: Added that line and merged. I'll coordinate a short blurb for release notes: "Docs: Retry-After header clarified (seconds per RFC); JS retry helper patched to treat values as seconds."

leo: Patch merged and published as v1.2.3. Pinging #sdk-updates.

sophie: Thanks team. I'll post a follow-up in #support with paste-ready snippets for customers who hit this. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
